topic: Sentence-level citation grounding for long-document question answering

selected_papers.title: SpanCite: Sentence-Level Citation Grounding for Long-Document QA
selected_papers.abstract: We propose SpanCite, a decoding-time constraint that requires each generated sentence to be traceable to a specific source span before it is emitted. On a long-document QA benchmark, SpanCite reduces the rate of unsupported claims in generated answers, at the cost of a small added latency overhead from the constrained decoding step. All experiments use English-language documents.

executive_summary.content: This review covers SpanCite, a method for keeping generated answers traceable to their sources in long documents [1].

introduction_scope.content: Retrieval is the step where a system finds relevant passages in a document collection. Faithfulness means a generated answer's claims are actually backed by what was retrieved, not invented by the model. This review covers exactly one paper, SpanCite, on improving faithfulness through constrained decoding.

thematic_findings.content: SpanCite constrains generation so that each sentence produced can be traced back to a specific passage in the source document, which improved faithfulness on a long-document QA benchmark [1].

methodology_landscape.content: SpanCite checks, at each sentence boundary, whether the sentence about to be generated can be tied to a specific retrieved span; if not, generation is redirected until a traceable sentence is produced [1].

contradictions_open_debates.content: As the only paper reviewed, SpanCite has no contradicting or corroborating work in this set to compare against.

gap_analysis.content: SpanCite's own evaluation is limited to English-language documents, and its abstract does not report the constrained decoding step's absolute latency cost [1].

future_research_directions.content: A natural next step is measuring SpanCite's constrained-decoding latency cost in absolute terms, since the paper reports only that a small cost exists, not its size [1].

conclusion.content: SpanCite's constrained decoding is a focused, single-mechanism approach to reducing unsupported claims in long-document answers [1].

refinement_context.notes: Every section is reworded (synonym-level paraphrase) but no claim, citation, mechanism, number, or structural element changes. Demonstrates that 'different prose' is not automatically improvement -- all seven dimensions stay unchanged even though revision_applied=true and every section's content differs.

citation_correctness.rationale: The same single reference is cited for the same claims in both versions; only the wording around each citation changed, not what is being claimed or which source is attached.

groundedness.rationale: Every factual claim in the refined version is the same claim as the draft's, just reworded -- no fact, number, or mechanism was added, removed, or altered.

synthesis_quality.rationale: This is a single-paper review in both versions; no cross-source synthesis claim exists to change.

analytical_quality.rationale: Gap Analysis and Future Research Directions retain the same diagnostic-vs-prescriptive relationship; only their wording differs.

template_fit.rationale: Foundational-appropriate depth/tone (defining retrieval/faithfulness before use) is preserved verbatim in structure, only reworded.

coherence.rationale: Section order, logical flow, and absence of repetition/illegitimate content are identical between versions.

source_balance.rationale: The single source is cited the same number of times, for the same claims, in both versions.
